name: Standard Account Structure
origin: Derived from the BetterPatio rebuild. Trevor's intended default for every managed account.
procedure: build_specs/NEW_ACCOUNT_SOP.md -- the ordered phases and the script for each. This file is the campaign model; that one is the order of operations.

account_level_setup.note: Set these ONCE per account, before any campaign is enabled. They are account-wide, so they also cover every campaign built later.

placement_exclusions.added: 2 October 2026, on Trevor's instruction after the client PMax campaigns were found serving heavily and untargeted on Display and YouTube.
placement_exclusions.mechanism: customer_negative_criterion. Since January 2026 these apply across Performance Max, Demand Gen, YouTube and Display simultaneously, so one list per account covers every campaign in it. PMax has no generally available channel off-switch and campaign.network_settings is NOT the lever.
placement_exclusions.script: scripts/apply_account_placement_exclusions.py (dry run by default, --execute to apply, idempotent)
placement_exclusions.evidence_first: scripts/audit_pmax_placements.py is read only and reports the network split and the actual placements. Feed specific sites/apps/channels back in with --placements FILE; do not guess them.
placement_exclusions.applies: 16 content labels (PARKED_DOMAIN and BELOW_THE_FOLD are the pure-waste pair) plus every mobile app category, resolved at run time from mobile_app_category_constant.
placement_exclusions.ui_path: Tools > Content suitability > Excluded content; Tools > Placement exclusion lists.

asset_automation.rule: Automatically-created assets stay OFF in every campaign, always. Set the opt-outs at campaign creation time, then sweep with scripts/disable_asset_automation_everywhere.py --execute.
asset_automation.channels: Only PERFORMANCE_MAX and SEARCH expose the setting.

account_level_setup.allowlist: Add the account to managed_accounts.json first. Both sweeps derive their account list from it, so that one edit enrols the account in every account-wide job.

the_model.principle: Three campaigns. PMax covers everything on the acquisition side; two remarketing campaigns split by intent.

destinations.product_ads: Product pages, supplied automatically by the Merchant Center feed

campaigns.why: One campaign serves Search, Shopping, Display, YouTube, Discover and Gmail. Replaces separate Search and Shopping campaigns entirely.

mandatory_settings.final_url_expansion: OFF — left on, Google routes traffic to pages of its own choosing, including collection pages. It silently undoes the landing page policy.
mandatory_settings.listing_group_filter: Filter to the categories with real image coverage rather than the whole catalogue.

campaigns.why: Static creative pulling warm traffic back to the quote funnel. On BetterPatio this is the best CPA in the account.

campaigns.destination: Product pages via the Merchant Center feed
campaigns.why: Shows viewers the exact products they browsed. Requires the feed linked to the campaign.
campaigns.common_failure: Pointing dynamic remarketing at the homepage instead of feed products. This was live on BetterPatio and is the likely cause of $291/mo producing zero conversions. Check this first on any account.

never: No ads pointing at collection pages — collections are for organic traffic.
No ads pointing at the homepage.
No separate Search or Shopping campaigns — PMax absorbs both.

prerequisites.product_feed: A linked Merchant Center account with an eligible product feed. Powers PMax product ads and dynamic remarketing.
prerequisites.funnel_page: A lead-gen / quote funnel page. Powers PMax search text ads and static remarketing. WITHOUT IT, two of the three campaigns have nowhere to send traffic.
prerequisites.images: Asset group images. Check the account's existing asset library first -- BetterPatio already held 766 usable images, so none needed sourcing.
prerequisites.conversion_tracking: Funnel path converts on lead form submission; product path needs a working purchase pixel. The funnel half is measurable even when purchase tracking is broken -- which is why it is the safer half to launch first.

account_readiness.note: Feed presence verified via the API. Funnel presence inferred from /pages/ URLs appearing in live ads -- an account may have a suitable page that simply is not being advertised yet.

eCommerce Paradise.status: TEMPLATE FITS AWKWARDLY — this is a services business (DFY builds, coaching, ads management), not a product retailer. The funnel half applies cleanly; the product half is questionable since there is little physical catalogue to sell. Likely wants funnel-led Search rather than PMax retail.

Laser Engraver Store.funnel: NO — no /pages/ URL in any ad
Laser Engraver Store.status: NEEDS FUNNEL PAGE. Note this account already has a strong SKAG structure worth preserving; the template would replace it, which may be the wrong trade here.

Fountains USA.funnel: NO — no /pages/ URL in any ad
Fountains USA.status: NEEDS FUNNEL PAGE. Otherwise a clean slate — every campaign is paused, nothing to disrupt.

Culinary Profis.funnel: NO — no /pages/ URL in any ad
Culinary Profis.status: NEEDS FUNNEL PAGE. Otherwise a clean slate — effectively an empty account.

rollout_blocker.issue: Three of five accounts have no funnel page: Laser Engraver Store, Fountains USA, Culinary Profis.
rollout_blocker.consequence: Two of the three template campaigns (PMax text ads, static remarketing) have no destination without one. Those accounts can only run the product half until a funnel exists.
rollout_blocker.note: Building these is squarely covered by the quote-request-home-page, b2b-quote-funnel and horizon-quote-store skills.

known_tradeoff: Folding Search into PMax gives up search-term visibility -- PMax reports at asset-group level, so the weekly search-term audit and negative-keyword workflow do not apply the same way. Accepted deliberately.
